trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum, and the whole point of this desk. It unlocks on its own the moment every other trophy on the list is in your collection, so there is nothing separate to hunt down. Plan the run with the roadmap view: campaign first, stranger strands next, then the long free-roam counts and collections. If one trophy ends up holding this back, it will almost always be the 100% completion gold or one of the big collectible sweeps.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Awarded for finishing Gone Fishing, the mission the campaign opens with. Play through the introduction and this pops as the mission wraps up; there is no optional condition attached to it. Because it is a required story beat, you cannot pass it by — everyone who starts the story earns it.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 1 of the campaign. Chapter trophies unlock automatically at the chapter's end, so steady story progress is all that is required. Nothing in the description adds a side condition, a difficulty setting or an optional objective.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 2. Like the other chapter trophies, this one is tied to plain story progression and unlocks at the chapter's conclusion. Keep following the campaign markers and it arrives on its own.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 3. It is awarded automatically when the third chapter closes. No optional objective is named in the description, so story progress alone earns it.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 4, the last of the numbered chapter trophies before the endgame. It unlocks as the chapter ends, so keep pushing the campaign forward and it will take care of itself.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Finish the final mission of the campaign — the gold that marks the end of the story. Expect it to unlock at the mission's conclusion. The description names no point of no return, but it does not promise free-roam cleanup afterwards either, so clear any missable-flagged trophies before you start the finale if you want to be completely safe.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run. Campaign missions are played in the order the story presents them, so this unlocks when that mission ends. The description names no optional condition or performance target.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Complete The Cartel Heist, a named campaign mission. Play the story until the heist is offered, finish it, and the trophy unlocks at the mission's end. Nothing in the description suggests a stealth, speed or no-deaths condition.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Complete Child's Play. A straight campaign-completion trophy: reach the mission in the story, finish it, and it pops. No side condition is stated in the description.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Complete Headliners. This is one of the named campaign missions, and it unlocks when the mission concludes. The description gives no extra requirement beyond completion.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Complete VCIA Takedown, the campaign mission set around VCIA, the airport. Finish the mission as the story presents it and the trophy is yours. If you are also chasing Catch Me If You Can, its description points at the same location, so keep an eye out while you are here.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Complete Operation Savage Glory. Another named campaign mission that unlocks on completion. Play it when the story offers it; no optional condition is named in the description.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Attain 100% completion — the long gold. This means finishing everything the game's completion counter tracks: the campaign, the stranger strands, the activities and the collectible sets on this list. Work through the roadmap stages in order and use the checklist to see what is left. The description does not list the counter's exact ingredients, so if you stall at 99%, sweep the categories with the smallest counts first — one missed activity type or card set is the usual suspect.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — the PSN progress target; guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts. Stunt opportunities are scattered through Leonida — jumps and set-piece moments the game counts as stunts. The description does not say whether repeating the same stunt counts, so vary your route and take every ramp the game offers rather than farming one spot until you know. This is a long count: start early and let it build alongside everything else.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — the PSN progress target; guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each type of activity once — PSN's target counts 9 activity types. Open the map, sample one of everything the game classes as an activity, and the trophy unlocks when the last type has been tried. You only need a taste of each, not a win, which makes this one of the quickest bronzes on the list. It also feeds the 100% completion counter, so do it early.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — the PSN progress target; guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges — 42 of them by PSN's target count. Treat this as a late-game skill trophy: learn each weapon's challenge first, then chase the gold score once you are comfortable with the game's shooting. The description does not name the ranges' locations, so unlock them as they appear on your map and clear them in batches.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — the PSN progress target; guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location — 14 locations on PSN's count. You need outright wins, not just entries, so learn each course's racing line before you count it done. The description does not list the locations; work through them as they surface on the map and tick them off here as you go.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — the PSN progress target; guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. Note the wording: different races, so repeating one easy event twenty times will not finish it. Enter every distinct race the map offers and take the win in each. Keep a tally in this checklist as you clear them, because the description gives no breakdown of which races you have already won.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — the PSN progress target; guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Find Cal's fishing challenge, enter it and out-fish him. The description does not say where Cal fishes or what the challenge scores, so treat the first meeting as a practice run if you need one. It is a one-off contest rather than a long count, so a single win settles it.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete an arcade game. Any one finished arcade game should do it — the description asks for a completion, not a high score. Arcades are part of Leonida's activity spread, so this pairs naturally with Master of None. Pick the shortest game you find and play it through to its end.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Andy — the end of Andy's stranger strand. Stranger strands are chains: work through each of Andy's missions as they appear until the last one is offered, then finish it. The description does not say where Andy is found, so pick his strand up whenever his marker shows. Finishing strands also counts toward Strangers & Freaks and the 100% completion gold.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Kenton, closing out Kenton's stranger strand. Work through his chain of missions as they unlock; the trophy pops when the last one is done. The description does not place Kenton on the map, so take his missions as they surface between story beats. His strand is one of the eight needed for Strangers & Freaks.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Billy — the last link in Billy's stranger strand. As with the other strangers, follow his missions in order until the finale is offered, then finish it. The description names no location for Billy, so sweep his strand up whenever you cross his marker. It counts toward both Strangers & Freaks and 100% completion.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida. Each strand is a short chain for one character — Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone have their own trophies on this list, and the description leaves room for more it does not name. Finishing a character's final mission completes their strand. Eight are needed, so explore between story missions and never leave a stranger marker sitting for long.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — the PSN progress target; guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Randy, the end of Randy's stranger strand. Play his missions in the order they are offered until the finale appears, then close it out. The description does not say where Randy operates, so grab his missions when his marker is nearby. The finished strand counts toward Strangers & Freaks.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Tyrone — the last job in Tyrone's stranger strand. Follow the chain from his first mission to his last; the trophy unlocks when the final one ends. The description gives no location for Tyrone, so work his strand whenever you are in his part of Leonida. One more strand toward the eight that Strangers & Freaks asks for.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every meditation spot across Leonida — 18 spots by PSN's count. These are fixed places in the world, so treat this as a collection sweep: visit each spot and use the meditation prompt when it appears. The description does not map the spots, so mark them off here as you find them, and expect a few to sit in out-of-the-way corners of the state.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — the PSN progress target; guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. Bret's request points you at one specific animal rather than a species count, so follow his strand until the hunt is offered and bring the animal down. The description does not name the animal or its hunting ground, so be ready for a tracking exercise when it comes. Because the hunt hangs off Bret's strand, keep his missions moving alongside the other strangers.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete 3 Collectible Card sets. Cards are found out in the world and grouped into sets, and three full sets means a lot of individual cards. The description does not say how many cards a set holds or where they hide, so search interiors and landmarks as you pass and log each set here as it completes. This is one of the longer collection grinds on the list — start it early and let it run in the background of everything else.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — the PSN progress target; guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: WAiNK It at 100 locations. The description leans on the game's own wording: there is a WAiNK action or spot type, and 100 of them are spread across Leonida. Treat it as a map-wide collection — use the prompt wherever it appears and keep your count here. The description does not define WAiNK beyond the name, so the first time the game offers the prompt, note what it was; the remaining 99 will look the same.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — the PSN progress target; guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 Challenges. Challenges are the game's bite-size objectives, and fifty completions is a mid-length count that builds naturally as you play everything else. The description does not list the challenge types, so dip into them whenever they are offered rather than saving them all for a cleanup session at the end.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — the PSN progress target; guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Lose a 4-star Wanted Level with your partner present and escape the heat. Build the wanted level up to four stars while your partner is with you, then break line of sight and stay hidden until the stars clear. The description stresses that your partner must be there, so do not attempt it solo. Open ground outside the city gives you the most room to vanish.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level in between. The chain is the hard part: move straight from shop to shop, keep the heat on you, and do not let the stars drop or the run resets. Plan a tight triangle of shops before you start, and have your escape route away from the third one ready.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — the PSN progress target; guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles. Vehicles are discovered by encountering them — driving one, or getting close enough for the game to register it. A hundred distinct vehicles is a long tail: vary the districts you drive through, because rich and poor areas stock different traffic. The description does not say whether entering a vehicle is required, so if your count stalls, start actually getting into new models rather than just passing them.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — the PSN progress target; guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus. You need a crowded fight: let five enemies group up, trigger Combat Focus once, and drop all five before it ends. The description does not say where such a fight is guaranteed, so story shootouts and gang operations are your best hunting grounds. If a run ends at four, reposition and try the next crowd rather than forcing it.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — the PSN progress target; guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA, the airport. The wording suggests leaving by air outside the story's schedule, and VCIA is also the setting of the campaign mission VCIA Takedown. Missable warning: the description does not confirm this can be done in free roam after that mission, so attempt it during VCIA Takedown itself — if a plane or a departure opportunity appears in that mission, take it. If it turns out to be free-roam only, following this advice costs you nothing.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: The description is a joke at face value — 'Kinda hot in these Rhinos' — and a Rhino is the game's tank. Read plainly, this trophy involves tanks, most likely surviving or dealing with them when the military shows up. The description states no kill count and no survival time, so we will not invent one: when you first meet a Rhino, engage with it and watch what the game counts. High wanted levels and military responses are the natural places to look.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. Pick a jewelry store, go in quietly, take what you came for and leave before anyone raises the alarm. The description sets the whole condition: no detection at any point. If you are spotted, walk away and try another store rather than finishing a blown attempt — only a clean run counts.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 Bank Vaults and escape. That is five separate vault robberies, each closed out by a successful escape — losing the heat afterwards is part of the trophy, not an extra. The description does not name the banks, so work the ones the game marks as you find them and log each escape here. By the fifth, a repeatable entry-and-exit pattern makes the run feel routine.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — the PSN progress target; guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an Armored Truck and escape. Armored trucks are the classic moving target: stop one, open it, take the money and lose the heat. The description does not say how the trucks are marked, so watch for them on the road as you drive. One successful robbery followed by a clean escape is enough.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida — 52 areas on PSN's count. This is the map-completion trophy: every named district and region needs a visit. Drive the whole state methodically, from the coast to the Keys to the northern wilds, and let this checklist's count guide the sweep. Areas usually register on entry, so one thorough road trip late in the game mops up whatever the story never showed you.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — the PSN progress target; guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang — 9 gangs on PSN's count. One operation per gang is enough; you do not need to clear every site on the map. The description does not name the gangs or their territories, so as each gang reveals itself through play, hit one of its operations and note it here. Variety, not volume, is the requirement.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — the PSN progress target; guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. The name — 'In The Beginning…' — points at the game's opening stretch, and Ocean Beach is where the story starts. Missable warning: the description does not say the moment can be repeated later, so when you are first on Ocean Beach early in the game, find the cocktail spot and take the drink before moving on. It costs a minute and removes the risk entirely.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style. 'In classic style' reads like a set-piece: driving a car out through the showroom's glass front. Missable warning: the description does not name a free-roam showroom where this can be repeated, so if a story mission puts you inside a vehicle showroom, take the loud way out when the chance appears. If you find a showroom in free roam first, the same exit should serve.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley — in plain terms, go bowling there. The description names the alley, which makes this one of the few trophies that tells you exactly where to go. Visit the alley, play your game, and complete the follow-through the game asks for. It should also register as an activity type toward Master of None.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: The description — 'A partnership with mass appeal' — is deliberately cryptic and pins down nothing we can honestly expand into steps. It clearly involves the two protagonists' partnership and some public-facing moment. Our advice is limited to this: trophies worded this way usually unlock during a story or partner activity, so play the campaign and the partner content and watch for it. We will not invent a location or a condition the description does not give.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Make choices — PSN's progress target counts to 500, so this is a cumulative tally of the choices the game offers across a full playthrough and beyond. Dialogue picks, mission decisions and small world choices all plausibly feed it, though the description does not itemise them. Five hundred is a lot: engage with optional conversations and decisions instead of skipping through them, and let the count build over the whole game.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — the PSN progress target; guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: 'Second time's the charm' — the honest reading is that something must fail once and then succeed on the retry. The description does not say what the something is, so we will not guess a specific event. If a retryable activity, challenge or encounter defeats you once, go straight back in: a success on the second attempt is the natural trigger for a trophy worded this way.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: 'What the hell just happened?' — a trophy for witnessing something strange. The description gives no place, no time and no event, and we will not invent one. Trophies worded like this usually hang on a scripted oddity somewhere in the world: explore off the main roads, especially at night, and pay attention when the game shows you something it refuses to explain.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by — knock a person down by striking them with a melee attack from a moving vehicle. You need speed, a pedestrian in reach and a melee swing timed as you pass. The description demands neither a kill nor a specific vehicle, so a slow pass with a melee weapon out of the window is the controlled way to line it up.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked bills come from scores that pay in dirty money; your contacts wash them, and this trophy tracks what you earn through that washing. The description does not name the contacts or their rate, so build the habit early: route dirty money through the laundering option whenever it appears instead of spending it raw.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — the PSN progress target; guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops. Any shop counts and the spending is cumulative, so this arrives naturally if you buy vehicles, clothes, weapons and services as you play. If you are close at the end of your run, one deliberate shopping spree finishes it — keep the running total in mind before the platinum push.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — the PSN progress target; guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase all garage properties — 8 of them on PSN's count. Garages are bought with in-game money, so this is partly an earnings trophy: keep your income ahead of the prices. The description does not list the garages' locations, so buy each one as it is offered and log it here. Owning them all also gives your vehicle collection somewhere to live.
trophies.sources: Sources: Exophase — the official trophy list (name, description and grade); PSNProfiles — the PSN progress target; guide text: our own advice drawn from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. When you find a vehicle worth keeping, register it through the app; ten registrations finish the trophy. The description does not say the vehicles must be different models, but registering ten distinct finds is the safe reading and costs little extra effort.
